section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Batch.Lift
/-!
# The digit-lifted sources and the count identity

The sources of a batch are 0/1 matrices with at most one entry 1 in each inner block of `p` columns.
A source row `ρ = (i K₀² + u) N₀ + o` belongs to the product `u` (`rowU`) and is its row
`R = i N₀ + o` (`rowR`).  The inner index `κ = cl p + r` is the vertex `cl` of the middle block and
the residue `r`.  The entry is 1 iff the triple `(u, R, cl)` is valid (`ok`) and `r` is the residue
`f u R cl`.

* `sum_srcVal`: the inner product of a row of the left source and a column of the right source of the
  same product counts the `cl` where both are valid and the two residues agree.
* `lift_count`: with the residues of the digit construction (Lemma 4.1 of the note), the residues
  agree iff `p` divides the triangle sum.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset

namespace ThreeSumApsp.Batch

/-- The product of a source row. -/
def rowU (KK N0 ρ : ℕ) : ℕ := ρ / N0 % KK

/-- The row of its product that a source row is. -/
def rowR (KK N0 ρ : ℕ) : ℕ := ρ / N0 / KK * N0 + ρ % N0

/-- The source row of the row `R` of the product `u`. -/
def srcOf (KK N0 u R : ℕ) : ℕ := (R / N0 * KK + u) * N0 + R % N0

/-- The entry `(ρ, κ)` of a source. -/
def srcVal (s p KK N0 : ℕ) (ok : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Bool) (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (ρ κ : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if κ / p < s ∧ ok (rowU KK N0 ρ) (rowR KK N0 ρ) (κ / p) = true ∧
      κ % p = f (rowU KK N0 ρ) (rowR KK N0 ρ) (κ / p) then 1 else 0

/-! ## The residues of the digit construction -/

/-- The residue of an integer, as a natural number. -/
def resid (p : ℕ) (w : ℤ) : ℕ := (w % (p : ℤ)).toNat

/-! ## The sources of the digit construction -/

section Digits

variable (n s p k T KK bt : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ)

/-- The product `u` of the batch `bt` is the product of the middle block `bt K₀² + u`. -/
abbrev jOf (u : ℕ) : ℕ := bt * KK + u

/-- The left source: row `R = a k + l` of the product of the middle block `j`, vertex `cl` of the
block; the residue is `(w(a, c) - l) mod p`. -/
def okX (u R cl : ℕ) : Bool := decide (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u < T ∧ R / k < n ∧ ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u * s + cl < n)

def fX (u R cl : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.resid p (AC.getD (R / k * n + (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u * s + cl)) 0) + (p - R % k) % p) % p

/-- The right source: column `C = b k + h`; the residue is `(h k - w(b, c)) mod p`. -/
def okY (u C cl : ℕ) : Bool := decide (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u < T ∧ C / k < n ∧ ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u * s + cl < n)

def fY (u C cl : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (C % k * k % p + ThreeSumApsp.Batch.resid p (-BC.getD (C / k * n + (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u * s + cl)) 0)) % p

end Digits

/-! ## The virtual positions of a query -/

/-- The virtual position of the row `R` of the slot row `g`. -/
def virt (K0 N0 g R : ℕ) : ℕ := R / N0 * (K0 * N0) + g * N0 + R % N0

end ThreeSumApsp.Batch
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter2.Defs
/-!
# Deterministic filtering: parameters and the counting oracle

The filtering reduction of the 2.996001 note (Lemma 3.1, Lemma 4.1).  A candidate is a triple
`(a, b, j)`: the pair `(a, b)` and the block `C_j = [j s, min((j+1) s, n))` of third vertices.  It
lies at index `i = j n² + a n + b`; its group is the pair, `i % (n n) = a n + b`.  For a modulus
`p ≥ 1` its count is the number of `c ∈ C_j` with `p ∣ w(a,b) + w(b,c) + w(a,c)`.

* The parameters, as functions of `n` and `U` (§3, (3.5)): `kOf`, `ellOf`, `RR`, `bOf`, `dOf`,
  `roundsOf`, `sOf`, `mOf`, `cKOf`, `rOf`, `BOf`, `hOf`, `pool`, `QOf`, `Guard`, `PmaxOf`.
* The counts (`cntList`) and the task of the counting oracle (`oracleTask`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter2

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

/-! ## Parameters -/

/-- `k`, the bit length of `n`: `n < 2^k`. -/
def kOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size n

/-- `ℓ = ⌊√k⌋ + 1`. -/
def ellOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt (Light.Filter2.kOf n) + 1

/-- `R = 2^ℓ`; the pool is the primes in `[R, 2R)`. -/
def RR (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ Light.Filter2.ellOf n

/-- `b = ℓ (⌊√ℓ⌋ + 1)`, about `k^{3/4}`. -/
def bOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Light.Filter2.ellOf n * (Nat.sqrt (Light.Filter2.ellOf n) + 1)

/-- `d = ⌊b/2⌋`: a round with the guard shrinks the active set by `2^d`. -/
def dOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Light.Filter2.bOf n / 2

/-- The number of rounds, `⌊3k/d⌋ + 1`, so that `d · rounds > 3k`. -/
def roundsOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 3 * Light.Filter2.kOf n / Light.Filter2.dOf n + 1

/-- The block size `s = 2^{⌊σ k⌋}`, `σ = 0.0336175`. -/
def sOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ (336175 * Light.Filter2.kOf n / 10 ^ 7)

/-- The number of blocks, `⌈n/s⌉`. -/
def mOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (n + Light.Filter2.sOf n - 1) / Light.Filter2.sOf n

/-- `c_K`, the bit length of the largest witness count `s`. -/
def cKOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size (Light.Filter2.sOf n)

/-- The number of prime factors per round, `⌊(c_K + b)/ℓ⌋ + 1`. -/
def rOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Light.Filter2.cKOf n + Light.Filter2.bOf n) / Light.Filter2.ellOf n + 1

/-- `B`, the bit length of `3U`: every triangle sum has absolute value below `2^B`. -/
def BOf (U : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size (3 * U)

/-- `h = ⌊(B − 1)/ℓ⌋`: a nonzero integer below `2^B` in absolute value has at most `h` prime
divisors in the pool. -/
def hOf (n U : ℕ) : ℕ := (Light.Filter2.BOf U - 1) / Light.Filter2.ellOf n

/-- The pool: the primes in `[R, 2R)`. -/
def pool (n : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (2 * Light.Filter2.RR n)).filter fun q => Light.Filter2.RR n ≤ q ∧ q.Prime

/-- `Q`, the size of the pool. -/
def QOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Light.Filter2.pool n).card

/-- The guard (3.6), `K (2h)^r 2^d ≤ Q^r` with `K = s`.  Not tested by the program on the main
path; it holds for all large `n` along polynomially bounded `U`. -/
def Guard (n U : ℕ) : Prop := Light.Filter2.sOf n * (2 * Light.Filter2.hOf n U) ^ Light.Filter2.rOf n * 2 ^ Light.Filter2.dOf n ≤ Light.Filter2.QOf n ^ Light.Filter2.rOf n

instance (n U : ℕ) : Decidable (Light.Filter2.Guard n U) := by unfold Light.Filter2.Guard; infer_instance

/-- The largest modulus, `(2R)^r`. -/
def PmaxOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (2 * Light.Filter2.RR n) ^ Light.Filter2.rOf n

/-! ## The counts -/

/-- The block `j` of third vertices: `c` with `j s ≤ c < (j + 1) s` and `c < n`. -/
def InBlock (n s j c : ℕ) : Prop := j * s ≤ c ∧ c < (j + 1) * s ∧ c < n

instance (n s j c : ℕ) : Decidable (Light.Filter2.InBlock n s j c) := by unfold Light.Filter2.InBlock; infer_instance

/-- The triangle sum `w(a,b) + w(b,c) + w(a,c)` of the pair `q = a n + b` and the vertex `c`, as in
`aeFlags`. -/
def triSum (n : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (q c : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  AB.getD q 0 + BC.getD (q % n * n + c) 0 + AC.getD (q / n * n + c) 0

/-- The count of the candidate `i = j n² + q` at the modulus `p`: the `c` in block `j` with
`p ∣ triSum q c`. -/
def cntOf (n s p : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range n).filter fun c =>
    Light.Filter2.InBlock n s (i / (n * n)) c ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ Light.Filter2.triSum n AB BC AC (i % (n * n)) c).card

/-- All `m n²` counts at the modulus `p`, candidate `i` in cell `i`. -/
def cntList (n s p : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) : List ℤ :=
  (List.range ((n + s - 1) / s * (n * n))).map fun i => (Light.Filter2.cntOf n s p AB BC AC i : ℤ)

/-! ## The counting oracle as a task -/

/-- An instance of the oracle: an all-edges instance (without the place of the flags), a block size
`s`, a modulus `p`, and the place `cnt` of the `m n²` counts. -/
structure OracleInst : Type extends TriInst where
  s : ℕ
  p : ℕ
  cnt : ℕ

/-- The number of counts, `⌈n/s⌉ n²`. -/
def OracleInst.len (x : Light.Filter2.OracleInst) : ℕ := (x.n + x.s - 1) / x.s * (x.n * x.n)

/-- The matrices and the place of the counts lie below the free pointer and do not meet;
`1 ≤ s ≤ n`, `1 ≤ p`. -/
structure OracleInst.Pre (x : Light.Filter2.OracleInst) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (fr : ℕ) : Prop
    extends TriInst.Pre x.toTriInst μ fr where
  s_pos : 1 ≤ x.s
  s_le : x.s ≤ x.n
  p_pos : 1 ≤ x.p
  belowCnt : x.cnt + x.len ≤ fr
  apartAB : Apart x.ab (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len
  apartBC : Apart x.bc (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len
  apartAC : Apart x.ac (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len

/-- **The counting oracle** (Lemma 4.1): `oracle(n, U, ab, bc, ac, s, p, cnt, fr)` writes the counts
of all candidates at the modulus `p` to `cnt`, and changes no other cell below `fr`. -/
def oracleTask : TaskN where
  Inst := Light.Filter2.OracleInst
  pars x := [x.n, x.U, x.s, x.p]
  args x := [x.n, x.U, x.ab, x.bc, x.ac, x.s, x.p, x.cnt]
  Pre := Light.Filter2.OracleInst.Pre
  Post x μ fr _ μ' := Seg μ' x.cnt (Light.Filter2.cntList x.n x.s x.p x.AB x.BC x.AC) ∧
    KeptBut μ μ' fr x.cnt x.len

end Light.Filter2
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Batch.OMath
/-!
# The batched counting oracle: the sources and the answer of a query

The two sources of a batch have the same shape (`srcMat`): the entry `(ρ, κ)` is 1 iff the product
`u` and the row `R` of the row `ρ`, and the vertex `cl = κ / p` of the middle block, are valid, and
`κ % p` is the residue `fGen T1 T2 u R cl = (T1[a n + c] + T2[l]) mod p` (`R = a k + l`,
`c = j s + cl`).  The left source has `T1 = w(a, c) mod p`, `T2[l] = -l mod p`; the right source,
transposed, has `T1 = -w(b, c) mod p`, `T2[h] = h k mod p`.

`query_eq_cntOf`: the query of the batched data structure at the virtual positions of the pair
`(a, b)` in the slot `(g, h)` returns the count of the candidate `j n² + a n + b`, `j` the middle
block of the product `u = g K₀ + h`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset ThreeSumApsp ThreeSumApsp.Batch ThreeSumApsp.Spec

namespace Light.Batch

/-- The residue of the cell of the row `R` and the vertex `cl`. -/
def fGen (n s p k KK bt : ℕ) (T1 T2 : ℕ → ℕ) (u R cl : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (T1 (R / k * n + (ThreeSumApsp.Batch.jOf KK bt u * s + cl)) + T2 (R % k)) % p

/-- A source of a batch, `rows × D`. -/
def srcMat (rows D' n s p k T KK N0 bt : ℕ) (T1 T2 : ℕ → ℕ) : Matrix (Fin rows) (Fin D') ℤ :=
  fun ρ κ => srcVal s p KK N0 (okX n s k T KK bt) (fGen n s p k KK bt T1 T2) ρ κ

/-- The tables of the left source. -/
def t1X (p : ℕ) (AC : List ℤ) (q : ℕ) : ℕ := ThreeSumApsp.Batch.resid p (AC.getD q 0)
def t2X (p : ℕ) (l : ℕ) : ℕ := (p - l) % p
/-- The tables of the right source. -/
def t1Y (p : ℕ) (BC : List ℤ) (q : ℕ) : ℕ := ThreeSumApsp.Batch.resid p (-BC.getD q 0)
def t2Y (p k : ℕ) (h : ℕ) : ℕ := h * k % p
end Light.Batch
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Batch.OSpecs
/-!
# The batched counting oracle: what its small procedures do

The specifications of the procedures 76 to 82 (`OProg`), as propositions about a program `P`, with
their times.  They are proved in `OTables` (the tables) and `OWrite` (writeSrc).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light.Batch

open ThreeSumApsp ThreeSumApsp.Batch Light.Sec4

/-! ## Times -/

def tPowNat (e : ℕ) : ℕ := 12 * e + 12
def tResidTab (len V p : ℕ) : ℕ := len * (emodTime V p + 30) + 10
def tSmallTab (len V p : ℕ) : ℕ := len * (emodTime V p + 30) + 10
def tRowTab (nb N0 : ℕ) : ℕ := nb * (N0 * 30 + 30) + 10
def tDivTab (k : ℕ) : ℕ := k * (k * 30 + 30) + 10
def tZTab (len : ℕ) : ℕ := len * 60 + 20
/-- writeSrc: the clearing of `sz` cells, then the products, rows and cells. -/
def tWriteSrc (sz KKb n k s : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  tFill sz + KKb * (n * (k * (s * 60 + 60) + 30) + 60) + 30

/-! ## Specifications -/

variable (lim : Limits) (P : Program)

/-- powNat(b, e) returns `b^e`, for `b ≥ 1`, and changes no cell. -/
def PowNatSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (b e : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ b → ((b ^ e + e + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ lim.word →
    Meets lim P pPowNat d [b, e] μ (tPowNat e) fun r μ' => r = (b ^ e : ℕ) ∧ μ' = μ

/-- residTab(dst, src, len, sgn, p, fr), `sgn = ±1`: `dst[q] := resid p (sgn · src[q])`.  It changes
the `len` cells from dst and cells from fr on (the table of emod). -/
def ResidTabSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (dst src : ℕ) (W : List ℤ) (sgn : ℤ) (p V fr : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ),
    (sgn = 1 ∨ sgn = -1) → Seg μ src W → (∀ w ∈ W, |w| ≤ V) → Emod.Pre lim p V fr →
    dst + W.length ≤ fr → src + W.length ≤ fr → Apart dst W.length src W.length →
    d + 1 ≤ lim.depth →
    Meets lim P pResidTab d [dst, src, W.length, sgn, p, fr] μ (tResidTab W.length V p)
      fun _ μ' => SegN μ' dst (W.map fun w => resid p (sgn * w)) ∧
        SameOn (fun b => b < fr ∧ Outside dst W.length b) μ μ'

/-- smallTab(dst, len, mul, add, p, fr): `dst[h] := resid p (h · mul + add)`. -/
def SmallTabSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (dst len : ℕ) (mul add : ℤ) (p V fr : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ),
    (∀ h < len, |(h : ℤ) * mul + add| ≤ V) → |mul| ≤ V → |add| ≤ V → (len : ℤ) ≤ V →
    Emod.Pre lim p V fr → dst + len ≤ fr → d + 1 ≤ lim.depth →
    Meets lim P pSmallTab d [dst, len, mul, add, p, fr] μ (tSmallTab len V p)
      fun _ μ' => SegN μ' dst ((List.range len).map fun h => resid p ((h : ℤ) * mul + add)) ∧
        SameOn (fun b => b < fr ∧ Outside dst len b) μ μ'

/-- rowTab(dst, nb, N0, Mul): `dst[R] := R / N0 · Mul + R % N0` for `R < nb N0`. -/
def RowTabSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (dst nb N0 Mul : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ), Std lim → 1 ≤ N0 → dst + nb * N0 < lim.space →
    (((nb + 1) * (Mul + N0 + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ lim.word →
    Meets lim P pRowTab d [dst, nb, N0, Mul] μ (tRowTab nb N0)
      fun _ μ' => SegN μ' dst ((List.range (nb * N0)).map fun R => R / N0 * Mul + R % N0) ∧
        SameOutside μ μ' dst (nb * N0)

/-- divTab(dst, k): `dst[z] := z / k` for `z < k²`. -/
def DivTabSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (dst k : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ), Std lim → dst + k * k < lim.space →
    Meets lim P pDivTab d [dst, k] μ (tDivTab k)
      fun _ μ' => SegN μ' dst ((List.range (k * k)).map fun z => z / k) ∧
        SameOutside μ μ' dst (k * k)

/-- zTab(zh, zl, rn, dk, len, k): `zh[q] := rn[q] / k`, `zl[q] := rn[q] % k`, from the table
`dk` of divTab. -/
def ZTabSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (zh zl rn dk k : ℕ) (RN : List ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ), Std lim → 1 ≤ k → SegN μ rn RN →
    SegN μ dk ((List.range (k * k)).map fun z => z / k) → (∀ z ∈ RN, z < k * k) →
    Apart zh RN.length zl RN.length → Apart zh RN.length rn RN.length →
    Apart zl RN.length rn RN.length → Apart zh RN.length dk (k * k) →
    zh + RN.length < lim.space → zl + RN.length < lim.space → rn + RN.length < lim.space →
    dk + k * k < lim.space →
    Meets lim P pZTab d [zh, zl, rn, dk, RN.length, k] μ (tZTab RN.length)
      fun _ μ' => SegN μ' zh (RN.map (· / k)) ∧ SegN μ' zl (RN.map (· % k)) ∧
        SameOn (fun b => Outside zh RN.length b ∧ Outside zl RN.length b) μ μ'

/-- What writeSrc assumes.  The source has `KK NP` rows of `D` cells from base; the tables T1
(`n²` residues) and T2 (`k` residues) and the table RS of the first rows `R / N0 · KK N0 + R % N0`
lie apart from it; the products `j0 + u`, `u < KKb`, have middle blocks that begin below `n`. -/
structure WriteSrcPre (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (base t1 t2 rs n k p D N0 j0 KKb s KK NP : ℕ) (T1 T2 : List ℕ) :
    Prop where
  std : Std lim
  p_pos : 1 ≤ p
  N0_pos : 1 ≤ N0
  k_pos : 1 ≤ k
  D_pos : 1 ≤ D
  seg1 : SegN μ t1 T1
  len1 : T1.length = n * n
  lt1 : ∀ x ∈ T1, x < p
  seg2 : SegN μ t2 T2
  len2 : T2.length = k
  lt2 : ∀ x ∈ T2, x < p
  segRS : SegN μ rs ((List.range NP).map fun R => R / N0 * (KK * N0) + R % N0)
  NP_mul : N0 ∣ NP
  nk_le : n * k ≤ NP
  KKb_le : KKb ≤ KK
  blocks : ∀ u < KKb, (j0 + u) * s < n
  sp_le : s * p ≤ D
  space : base + KK * NP * D < lim.space
  apart1 : Apart base (KK * NP * D) t1 (n * n)
  apart2 : Apart base (KK * NP * D) t2 k
  apartRS : Apart base (KK * NP * D) rs NP
  below1 : t1 + n * n < lim.space
  below2 : t2 + k < lim.space
  belowRS : rs + NP < lim.space
  word : (((j0 + KKb + 1) * (s + 1) + n * n + n * k + 2 * p + 4 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ lim.word

/-- writeSrc(base, t1, t2, rs, n, k, p, D, N0, j0, KKb, s, KK NP D): afterwards the `KK NP × D`
source at base holds `srcMat` for the batch `bt` (`j0 = bt KK`, the valid products `u < KKb`), and
no other cell has changed. -/
def WriteSrcSpec : Prop :=
  ∀ (base t1 t2 rs n k p D N0 bt KKb s KK NP : ℕ) (T1 T2 : List ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (d : ℕ),
    WriteSrcPre lim μ base t1 t2 rs n k p D N0 (bt * KK) KKb s KK NP T1 T2 →
    d + 1 ≤ lim.depth →
    Meets lim P pWriteSrc d [base, t1, t2, rs, n, k, p, D, N0, bt * KK, KKb, s, KK * NP * D] μ
      (tWriteSrc (KK * NP * D) KKb n k s) fun _ μ' =>
      (∀ ρ < KK * NP, ∀ κ < D, μ' (base + ρ * D + κ) =
        srcVal s p KK N0 (okX n s k (bt * KK + KKb) KK bt)
          (fGen n s p k KK bt (fun q => T1.getD q 0) (fun l => T2.getD l 0)) ρ κ) ∧
      SameOutside μ μ' base (KK * NP * D)

end Light.Batch
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Batch.OQuery
/-!
# The batched counting oracle: the queries of a batch

`queries(b0, ZL, ZH, RV, n, k, N0, K0, KKb, cnt, j0)` asks, for each product `u < KKb` of the batch
(slot `g = u / K₀`, `h = u % K₀`) and each pair `(a, b)`, the query at the virtual positions
`I = virt g (a k + ZL[a n + b])`, `J = virt h (b k + ZH[a n + b])`, and stores the answer at
`cnt + (j0 + u) n² + a n + b` (`queries_ok`).  The invariant `QInv E`: the data structure is ready,
the first `E` cells from `cnt + j0 n²` hold their answers, and no other cell below b0 has changed.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light.Batch

open ThreeSumApsp ThreeSumApsp.Spec ThreeSumApsp.Batch Light.Sec4 QS

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-- The answer of the query of the pair `(a, b)` in the slot `(g, h)`. -/
def qVal (pv : Sec2.Par) (t : ℕ) (hmL : pv.m ≤ pv.L) (AL : ArrL pv) (AR : Light.Batch.ArrR pv) (n k : ℕ)
    (ZL ZH : List ℕ) (g h a b : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  queryValue pv.m t
    (encRowA AL (virt pv.K0 pv.N0 g (a * k + ZL.getD (a * n + b) 0) / (pv.K0 * pv.N0)))
    (encColA AR (virt pv.K0 pv.N0 h (b * k + ZH.getD (a * n + b) 0) / (pv.K0 * pv.N0)))
    (outStrOfPos (stdLayout hmL) (virt pv.K0 pv.N0 g (a * k + ZL.getD (a * n + b) 0))
      (virt pv.K0 pv.N0 h (b * k + ZH.getD (a * n + b) 0)))

/-- The answer of the cell `e` from `cnt + j0 n²`. -/
def qAns (pv : Sec2.Par) (t : ℕ) (hmL : pv.m ≤ pv.L) (AL : ArrL pv) (AR : Light.Batch.ArrR pv) (n k : ℕ)
    (ZL ZH : List ℕ) (e : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  qVal pv t hmL AL AR n k ZL ZH (e / (n * n) / pv.K0) (e / (n * n) % pv.K0) (e % (n * n) / n)
    (e % (n * n) % n)

/-- What the queries of a batch assume, in the memory μ₀ at the start. -/
structure QSet (lim : Limits) (P : Program) (pv : Sec2.Par) (t : ℕ) (aX aY b0 : ℕ) (AL : ArrL pv)
    (AR : Light.Batch.ArrR pv) (U : ℤ) (μ₀ : ℕ → ℤ) (zl zh rv n k NP KKb cnt j0 : ℕ) (ZL ZH : List ℕ) :
    Prop where
  hq : QueryAtASpec lim P
  ht : t ≤ pv.m
  hlim : Lim30 lim pv t b0 U
  hb : BoundA AL AR U
  segZL : SegN μ₀ zl ZL
  segZH : SegN μ₀ zh ZH
  lenZL : ZL.length = n * n
  lenZH : ZH.length = n * n
  ltZL : ∀ x ∈ ZL, x < k
  ltZH : ∀ x ∈ ZH, x < k
  segRV : SegN μ₀ rv ((List.range NP).map fun R => R / pv.N0 * (pv.K0 * pv.N0) + R % pv.N0)
  hN : pv.N = pv.K0 * NP
  n_pos : 1 ≤ n
  NP_mul : pv.N0 ∣ NP
  nk_le : n * k ≤ NP
  KKb_le : KKb ≤ pv.K0 * pv.K0
  belowZL : zl + n * n ≤ b0
  belowZH : zh + n * n ≤ b0
  belowRV : rv + NP ≤ b0
  belowCnt : cnt + (j0 + KKb) * (n * n) ≤ b0
  apZL : Apart (cnt + j0 * (n * n)) (KKb * (n * n)) zl (n * n)
  apZH : Apart (cnt + j0 * (n * n)) (KKb * (n * n)) zh (n * n)
  apRV : Apart (cnt + j0 * (n * n)) (KKb * (n * n)) rv NP

/-- The invariant: the data structure is ready, the first `E` cells from `cnt + j0 n²` hold their
answers, and no other cell below b0 has changed. -/
def QInv (pv : Sec2.Par) (t : ℕ) (hmL : pv.m ≤ pv.L) (aX aY b0 : ℕ) (AL : ArrL pv) (AR : Light.Batch.ArrR pv)
    (μ₀ : ℕ → ℤ) (n k : ℕ) (ZL ZH : List ℕ) (base E : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
  DSReadyA pv t aX aY b0 AL AR μ ∧ (∀ e < E, μ (base + e) = qAns pv t hmL AL AR n k ZL ZH e) ∧
    ∀ x < b0, (x < base ∨ base + E ≤ x) → μ x = μ₀ x

/-- The time of the queries of a batch. -/
def tQueries (KKb n tq : ℕ) : ℕ := KKb * (n * (n * (tq + 80) + 20) + 80) + 30

section cell

variable {pv : Sec2.Par} {t : ℕ} {aX aY b0 : ℕ} {AL : ArrL pv} {AR : ArrR pv} {U : ℤ}
  {μ₀ : ℕ → ℤ} {zl zh rv n k NP KKb cnt j0 : ℕ} {ZL ZH : List ℕ}

/-- The locals of queries. -/
abbrev qFr (b0 zl zh rv n k N0 K0 KKb cnt j0 g h a b : ℕ) (I J r : ℤ) (dst u : ℕ) : List ℤ :=
  [b0, zl, zh, rv, n, k, N0, K0, KKb, cnt, j0, g, h, a, b, I, J, r, dst, u]

/-- The time of the queries of a row `a`. -/
def tQRow (n tq : ℕ) : ℕ := n * (tq + 80) + 6

/-- The time of the queries of a product. -/
def tQRows (n tq : ℕ) : ℕ := n * (tQRow n tq + 10) + 6

/-- The time of a product. -/
def tQProd (n tq : ℕ) : ℕ := tQRows n tq + 60

end cell

end Light.Batch
end
end

records.theorem_title: APSP in $O(n^{2.996001})$: definitions, part 2 of 2
records.natural_language_statement:
Definitions for the formal proof that all-pairs shortest paths can be solved deterministically in time $O(n^{2.996001})$ on a word RAM, part 2 of 2. It imports `APSP2996001_Defs1`.

This part contains the filtering host: the environment and the memory invariants of a step and of a round (`Env`, `FMem`, `Inv1`, `Inv2`), the bodies and times of a step, a round, the core and the top procedure (`tStep`, `tRound`, `tTop`), and the time `filterTime` and need `filterNeed` of the whole host.

Source modules (in this order): `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostFinal`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostStep`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostRound`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostCore`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostTop`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostAssemble`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostMain`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostTime`.

The bundles belong to the formal proof of the deterministic bound $O(n^{2.996001})$ for APSP (the filtering reduction of the 2.996001 note):

1. the pruned thin product of the 2.99791 entry at the new parameters $c=212733/10000$, $\theta=111731/10^6$, in the regime $D^{1249}\le N^{71}$, giving #Lop-AE-SparseTri (counting) in time $O(n^2\log^2D/D^{0.0703531}+wD^{0.4296471}\log D+nD+w)$;
2. the modular counting oracle of Lemma 4.1: for a block size $s$ and a modulus $p$ it computes, for every pair $(a,b)$ and every block $C_j$ of $s$ third vertices, the number of $c\in C_j$ with $p\mid w(a,b)+w(b,c)+w(a,c)$, by #Lop-AE-SparseTri calls at inner dimension $sp$;
3. the deterministic filtering host (Lemma 3.1): rounds of prime moduli from a pool of primes in $[R,2R)$ that certify the pairs with an exact triangle and shrink the set of active candidates, followed by a final check, solving All-Edges Exact Triangle, and the chain to APSP.

-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostFinal
/-!
# The filtering host: the last phase

For every group `g` that is not done, the blocks of its active candidates are scanned
(`groupBody`); the flag of `g` is 1 if it is done or a scan finds a zero triangle.  The time depends
on the number of active candidates (`final_spec`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-! ## Counting loops whose rounds take different times -/

/-! ## The scan of a block -/

/-- The scan of the block `j` for the pair of the group `g`. -/
def blockHit (n s : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (j g : ℕ) : Bool :=
  scanHit n AB BC AC (g / n) (g % n) (j * s) (min s (n - j * s))

/-! ## One group -/

/-- One block of the group.  Locals: 0 n, 1 ab, 2 bc, 3 ac, 4 out, 5 done, 6 act, 7 s, 8 m, 9 N,
10 a, 11 b, 12 g, 13 hit, 14 j, 15 c0, 16 len. -/
def groupRound (pScan : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .ite (Light.v 13 =' Light.k 0)
    (.ite (M (Light.v 6 +' Light.v 14 *' Light.v 9 +' Light.v 12) =' Light.k 0) .skip
      (.set 15 (Light.v 14 *' Light.v 7) ;;
       .set 16 (Light.v 7) ;;
       .ite (Light.v 0 -' Light.v 15 <' Light.v 7) (.set 16 (Light.v 0 -' Light.v 15)) .skip ;;
       .call pScan [Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 0, Light.v 10, Light.v 11, Light.v 15, Light.v 16] 13))
    .skip

/-- group(n, ab, bc, ac, out, done, act, s, m, N, a, b, g): the flag of the group `g = a n + b`. -/
def groupBody (pScan : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .set 13 (M (Light.v 5 +' Light.v 12)) ;;
  Stmt.for 14 (Light.v 8) (groupRound pScan) ;;
  .store (Light.v 4 +' Light.v 12) (Light.v 13) ;;
  .set 0 (Light.k 0)

/-- The flag of the group `g` after the first `j` blocks. -/
def hitB (n s : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (g j : ℕ) : Bool :=
  D g || (List.range j).any fun j' => act (j' * (n * n) + g) && blockHit n s AB BC AC j' g

/-- The number of active candidates of a group that is not done. -/
def cntG (N m : ℕ) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (g : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range m, if (act (j * N + g) && !D g) then 1 else 0

/-- The time of group. -/
def tGroup (m s c : ℕ) : ℕ := 60 * m + 20 + c * tScan s

/-! ## All groups -/

/-- final(n, ab, bc, ac, out, done, act, s, m, N): the flags of all groups.
Locals: 0 n, 1 ab, 2 bc, 3 ac, 4 out, 5 done, 6 act, 7 s, 8 m, 9 N, 10 a, 11 b, 12 g, 13 r. -/
def finalBody (pGroup : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  Stmt.for 12 (Light.v 9) (
    .call pGroup [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.v 6, Light.v 7, Light.v 8, Light.v 9, Light.v 10, Light.v 11, Light.v 12] 13 ;;
    .set 11 (Light.v 11 +' Light.k 1) ;;
    .ite (Light.v 11 =' Light.v 0) (.set 11 (Light.k 0) ;; .set 10 (Light.v 10 +' Light.k 1)) .skip) ;;
  .set 0 (Light.k 0)

/-- The time of final, with `c` the number of active candidates of the groups that are not done. -/
def tFinal (N m s c : ℕ) : ℕ := N * (60 * m + 60) + c * tScan s + 10

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostStep
/-!
# The filtering host: the layout, and one step of a round

* The layout of the memory of the host above the free pointer `fr`: the primes below `2R`, the pool,
  the marks `act` of the `L = m n²` candidates, the flags `done` of the `n²` groups, the masses `ua`
  of the groups, the counts `cnt` of the oracle, the table `gt` of the masses at the moduli `M q`,
  and the free pointer `top` of the oracle.
* `Env`: what the host knows about the limits and the instance; `FMem`: the memory between the
  steps.
* `stepBody`: one step of a round (`step_spec`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits}

/-! ## The layout -/

/-- The number of candidates, `m n²`. -/
def LL (n : ℕ) : ℕ := mOf n * (n * n)

/-- The pool. -/
def aPL (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := fr + 2 * RR n
/-- The marks of the candidates. -/
def aACT (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := fr + 4 * RR n
/-- The flags of the groups. -/
def aDONE (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := aACT n fr + Light.Filter.LL n
/-- The masses of the groups at the current modulus. -/
def aUA (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := aDONE n fr + n * n
/-- The counts written by the oracle. -/
def aCNT (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := aUA n fr + n * n
/-- The table of the masses at the moduli `M q`. -/
def aGT (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := aCNT n fr + Light.Filter.LL n
/-- The free pointer of the oracle (and the table of the sieve). -/
def aTOP (n fr : ℕ) : ℕ := aGT n fr + 2 * RR n * (n * n)

/-- The largest time of the oracle at the moduli up to `Pmax`. -/
def supTo (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (PmaxOf n + 1)).sup fun p => To [n, U, sOf n, p]

/-- A bound on the numbers that the host forms. -/
def filterWord (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  10 ^ 9 * ((n + 1) ^ 3 * (U + 1) * (RR n + 1) * (PmaxOf n + 1)) ^ 2

/-- What the host knows: the instance (in the first memory `μ0`), the limits, and the need of the
oracle at all moduli up to `Pmax`.  The host runs at depth `d`. -/
structure Env (lim : Limits) (d : ℕ) (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ0 : ℕ → ℤ) (needo : List ℕ → Light.Need) :
    Prop where
  pre : x.Pre μ0 fr
  hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word
  space : aTOP x.n fr + 2 * RR x.n ≤ lim.space
  word : (filterWord x.n x.U : ℤ) ≤ lim.word
  oracle : ∀ p ≤ PmaxOf x.n, (needo [x.n, x.U, sOf x.n, p]).Ok lim (aTOP x.n fr) (d + 4)
  depth : d + 5 ≤ lim.depth

/-- The memory between two steps: nothing below `fr` has changed, and the pool, the marks `act` and
the flags `D` are in place. -/
structure FMem (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ0 μ : ℕ → ℤ) (act D : ℕ → Bool) : Prop where
  kept : Light.Kept μ0 μ fr
  pool : Light.Filter.Arr μ (aPL x.n fr) (QOf x.n) fun t => (poolAt x.n t : ℤ)
  act : Light.Filter.Arr μ (aACT x.n fr) (Light.Filter.LL x.n) fun i => bitB (act i)
  done : Light.Filter.Arr μ (aDONE x.n fr) (x.n * x.n) fun g => bitB (D g)

/-- The masses of the groups that are not done, at the modulus `M`. -/
def UOk (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (M : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g < x.n * x.n, D g = false →
    μ (aUA x.n fr + g) = (mass x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC act M g : ℤ)

/-- The instance of the oracle at the modulus `p`. -/
def oInst (x : AEInst) (fr p : ℕ) : OracleInst :=
  { toTriInst := x.toTriInst, s := sOf x.n, p := p, cnt := aCNT x.n fr }

/-! ## Bounds on the numbers -/

/-- The product behind `filterWord`. -/
def KW (n U : ℕ) : ℕ := (n + 1) ^ 3 * (U + 1) * (RR n + 1) * (PmaxOf n + 1)

/-! ## Keeping the memory -/

section keep

variable {x : AEInst} {fr : ℕ} {μ0 μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ} {act D : ℕ → Bool} {M : ℕ}

/-- The table of the masses at the moduli `M q`, for the first `t` primes of the pool. -/
def GOk (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (act : ℕ → Bool) (M t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t' < t, ∀ g < x.n * x.n, μ (aGT x.n fr + (t' * (x.n * x.n) + g)) =
    (mass x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC act (M * poolAt x.n t') g : ℤ)

end keep

/-! ## One step -/

/-- step(n, U, ab, bc, ac, s, pl, act, done, ua, cnt, gt, top, N, m, Q, h, M): the oracle at every
`M q`, the certificate, the choice of `q*`; it returns `M q*`.  Locals: 18 t, 19 scratch, 20 the
row `t*`. -/
def stepBody (pO pAggr pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  Stmt.for 18 (Light.v 15) (
    .call pO [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.v 17 *' M (Light.v 6 +' Light.v 18), Light.v 10, Light.v 12] 19 ;;
    .call pAggr [Light.v 10, Light.v 7, Light.v 11 +' Light.v 18 *' Light.v 13, Light.v 13, Light.v 14] 19) ;;
  .call pCert [Light.v 9, Light.v 11, Light.v 8, Light.v 13, Light.v 15, Light.v 16] 19 ;;
  .call pArg [Light.v 11, Light.v 8, Light.v 13, Light.v 15] 20 ;;
  .call pCopy [Light.v 11 +' Light.v 20 *' Light.v 13, Light.v 9, Light.v 13] 19 ;;
  .set 0 (Light.v 17 *' M (Light.v 6 +' Light.v 20))

/-- The arguments of step. -/
def stepArgs (x : AEInst) (fr M : ℕ) : List ℤ :=
  [x.n, x.U, x.ab, x.bc, x.ac, sOf x.n, aPL x.n fr, aACT x.n fr, aDONE x.n fr, aUA x.n fr,
    aCNT x.n fr, aGT x.n fr, aTOP x.n fr, ((x.n * x.n : ℕ) : ℤ), mOf x.n, QOf x.n, hOf x.n x.U, M]

/-- The time of step. -/
def tStep (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  QOf n * (supTo To n U + tAggr (n * n) (mOf n) + 40) + tCert (n * n) (QOf n) +
    tArgmin (n * n) (QOf n) + copyTime (n * n) + 60

/-- The procedures that step calls. -/
structure StepProcs (P : Program) (pAggr pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ) : Prop where
  aggr : P[pAggr]? = some aggrBody
  cert : P[pCert]? = some certBody
  arg : P[pArg]? = some argminBody
  copy : P[pCopy]? = some copyBody

instance (n s U : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (act : ℕ → Bool) (M g : ℕ) :
    Decidable (certOf n s U AB BC AC act M g) := by
  unfold certOf; infer_instance

section step

variable {P₀ R : Program} {pO pAggr pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ} {To : List ℕ → ℕ}
  {needo : List ℕ → Need} {d0 : ℕ} {x : AEInst} {fr : ℕ} {μ0 : ℕ → ℤ}

/-- The flags after the certificate of a step at the modulus `Mc`. -/
def stepD (x : AEInst) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (Mc : ℕ) : ℕ → Bool := fun g =>
  D g || decide (∀ t < QOf x.n, hOf x.n x.U * mass x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC act Mc g <
    QOf x.n * mass x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC act (Mc * poolAt x.n t) g)

/-- The remaining mass at the modulus `M`, outside the groups that are done. -/
def remMass (x : AEInst) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (M : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ g ∈ Finset.range (x.n * x.n), if D g then 0 else mass x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC act M g

end step

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostRound
/-!
# The filtering host: one round

A round: the masses at the modulus `1`, then `r` steps, each of which certifies some groups and
multiplies the modulus by a prime of the pool, and at the end the marks of the candidates whose
count at the final modulus is `0` are cleared (`round_spec`).

The invariants: a group that is done has a witness (`Inv1`), and every candidate of a group that is
not done whose block has a witness is marked (`Inv2`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits}

/-- A group that is done has a witness. -/
def Inv1 (x : AEInst) (D : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ g < x.n * x.n, D g = true → ∃ c < x.n, triSum x.n x.AB x.BC x.AC g c = 0

/-- A candidate of a group that is not done, whose block has a witness, is marked. -/
def Inv2 (x : AEInst) (act D : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ i < Light.Filter.LL x.n, D (i % (x.n * x.n)) = false → 0 < cntOf x.n (sOf x.n) 0 x.AB x.BC x.AC i →
    act i = true

/-- round(n, U, ab, bc, ac, s, pl, act, done, ua, cnt, gt, top, N, m, Q, h, r).  Locals: 18 the
modulus `M`, 19 the step, 20 scratch. -/
def roundBody (pO pAggr pStep pFA : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .call pO [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.k 1, Light.v 10, Light.v 12] 20 ;;
  .call pAggr [Light.v 10, Light.v 7, Light.v 9, Light.v 13, Light.v 14] 20 ;;
  .set 18 (Light.k 1) ;;
  Stmt.for 19 (Light.v 17) (.call pStep [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.v 6, Light.v 7, Light.v 8, Light.v 9, Light.v 10, Light.v 11,
    Light.v 12, Light.v 13, Light.v 14, Light.v 15, Light.v 16, Light.v 18] 18) ;;
  .call pO [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.v 18, Light.v 10, Light.v 12] 20 ;;
  .call pFA [Light.v 7, Light.v 10, Light.v 14 *' Light.v 13] 20

/-- The time of round. -/
def tRound (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  2 * supTo To n U + tAggr (n * n) (mOf n) + rOf n * (tStep To n U + 58) + tFilterAct (Light.Filter.LL n) + 200

/-- The locals of round. -/
def rFrame (x : AEInst) (fr Mc st : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : List ℤ :=
  stepArgs x fr (rOf x.n) ++ [(Mc : ℤ), (st : ℤ), z]

/-- The procedures that round calls. -/
structure RoundProcs (P : Program) (pO pAggr pStep pFA pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ) : Prop where
  step : P[pStep]? = some (stepBody pO pAggr pCert pArg pCopy)
  sp : StepProcs P pAggr pCert pArg pCopy
  fa : P[pFA]? = some filterActBody

section round

variable {P₀ R : Program} {pO pAggr pStep pFA pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ} {To : List ℕ → ℕ}
  {needo : List ℕ → Need} {d0 : ℕ} {x : AEInst} {fr : ℕ} {μ0 : ℕ → ℤ}

/-- The invariant of the loop over the steps. -/
def StepInv (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ0 : ℕ → ℤ) (act D : ℕ → Bool) (st : ℕ) (σ : State) : Prop :=
  ∃ (Mc : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (D' : ℕ → Bool) (μ' : ℕ → ℤ), σ = ⟨Light.frame (rFrame x fr Mc st z), μ'⟩ ∧
    FMem x fr μ0 μ' act D' ∧ UOk x fr μ' act D' Mc ∧ 1 ≤ Mc ∧ Mc ≤ (2 * RR x.n) ^ st ∧
    Inv1 x D' ∧ (∀ g, D g = true → D' g = true) ∧
    QOf x.n ^ st * tot x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC (eff (x.n * x.n) act D') Mc ≤
      (2 * hOf x.n x.U) ^ st * tot x.n (sOf x.n) x.AB x.BC x.AC (eff (x.n * x.n) act D) 1

end round

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostCore
/-!
# The filtering host: the rounds and the final scans

`core` runs the rounds and then scans the blocks of the candidates that are still marked, in the
groups that are not done (`core_spec`).  The flags it writes are the flags of all-edges Exact
Triangle, whatever the guard; with the guard, no candidate is marked after the rounds, so that the
final scans cost nothing.
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits}

/-! ## The flags -/

/-! ## The program -/

/-- core(n, U, ab, bc, ac, s, pl, act, done, ua, cnt, gt, top, N, m, Q, h, r, rounds, out).  Locals:
20 the round, 21 scratch. -/
def coreBody (pRound pFinal : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  Stmt.for 20 (Light.v 18) (.call pRound [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 5, Light.v 6, Light.v 7, Light.v 8, Light.v 9, Light.v 10, Light.v 11,
    Light.v 12, Light.v 13, Light.v 14, Light.v 15, Light.v 16, Light.v 17] 21) ;;
  .call pFinal [Light.v 0, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 19, Light.v 8, Light.v 7, Light.v 5, Light.v 14, Light.v 13] 21 ;;
  .set 0 (Light.k 0)

/-- The arguments of core. -/
def coreArgs (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) : List ℤ :=
  stepArgs x fr (rOf x.n) ++ [(roundsOf x.n : ℤ), (x.out : ℤ)]

/-- The number of candidates that the final scans may meet: none with the guard, all without. -/
def cFin (n U : ℕ) : ℕ := if Guard n U then 0 else Light.Filter.LL n

/-- The time of core. -/
def tCore (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  roundsOf n * (Light.Filter.tRound To n U + 30) + tFinal (n * n) (mOf n) (sOf n) (cFin n U) + 30

/-- The procedures of the final scans. -/
structure FinalProcs (P : Program) (pFinal pGroup pScan : ℕ) : Prop where
  final : P[pFinal]? = some (finalBody pGroup)
  group : P[pGroup]? = some (groupBody pScan)
  scan : P[pScan]? = some scanBody

section core

variable {P₀ R : Program} {pO pAggr pStep pFA pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ} {To : List ℕ → ℕ}
  {needo : List ℕ → Need} {d0 : ℕ} {x : AEInst} {fr : ℕ} {μ0 : ℕ → ℤ}

/-- The invariant of the rounds. -/
def CoreInv (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) (μ0 : ℕ → ℤ) (ρ : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ act D : ℕ → Bool, FMem x fr μ0 μ act D ∧ Inv1 x D ∧ Inv2 x act D ∧
    (Guard x.n x.U → 2 ^ (dOf x.n * ρ) * cardA x.n (sOf x.n) (eff (x.n * x.n) act D) ≤ Light.Filter.LL x.n)

end core

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostTop
/-!
# The filtering host: the parameters

The first part of the host computes the parameters of the filtering from `n` and `U` and lays out
the memory above the free pointer (`params_spec`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits}

/-! ## The computation of the parameters -/

/-- The parameters, from `n` (local 0), `U` (local 1) and the free pointer (local 6): 7 `k`, 8 `ℓ`,
9 `R`, 10 `b`, 11 `d`, 12 the number of rounds, 13 `s`, 14 `m`, 15 `c_K`, 16 `r`, 17 `B`, 18 `h`,
19 `N = n²`, and the places 20 `pl`, 21 `act`, 22 `done`, 23 `ua`, 24 `cnt`, 25 `gt`, 26 `top`. -/
def paramsStmt (pLog pSqrt pPow pDiv : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .call pLog [Light.v 0] 7 ;; .set 7 (Light.v 7 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pSqrt [Light.v 7] 8 ;; .set 8 (Light.v 8 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pPow [Light.v 8] 9 ;;
  .call pSqrt [Light.v 8] 10 ;; .set 10 (Light.v 8 *' (Light.v 10 +' Light.k 1)) ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.v 10, Light.k 2] 11 ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.k 3 *' Light.v 7, Light.v 11] 12 ;; .set 12 (Light.v 12 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.k 284225 *' Light.v 7, Light.k 10000000] 13 ;; .call pPow [Light.v 13] 13 ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.v 0 +' Light.v 13 -' Light.k 1, Light.v 13] 14 ;;
  .call pLog [Light.v 13] 15 ;; .set 15 (Light.v 15 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.v 15 +' Light.v 10, Light.v 8] 16 ;; .set 16 (Light.v 16 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pLog [Light.k 3 *' Light.v 1] 17 ;; .set 17 (Light.v 17 +' Light.k 1) ;;
  .call pDiv [Light.v 17 -' Light.k 1, Light.v 8] 18 ;;
  .set 19 (Light.v 0 *' Light.v 0) ;;
  .set 20 (Light.v 6 +' Light.k 2 *' Light.v 9) ;;
  .set 21 (Light.v 6 +' Light.k 4 *' Light.v 9) ;;
  .set 22 (Light.v 21 +' Light.v 14 *' Light.v 19) ;;
  .set 23 (Light.v 22 +' Light.v 19) ;;
  .set 24 (Light.v 23 +' Light.v 19) ;;
  .set 25 (Light.v 24 +' Light.v 14 *' Light.v 19) ;;
  .set 26 (Light.v 25 +' Light.k 2 *' Light.v 9 *' Light.v 19)

/-- The locals after the parameters. -/
def topFrame (x : AEInst) (fr : ℕ) : List ℤ :=
  [x.n, x.U, x.ab, x.bc, x.ac, x.out, fr, kOf x.n, ellOf x.n, RR x.n, bOf x.n, dOf x.n,
    roundsOf x.n, sOf x.n, mOf x.n, cKOf x.n, rOf x.n, BOf x.U, hOf x.n x.U, ((x.n * x.n : ℕ) : ℤ),
    aPL x.n fr, aACT x.n fr, aDONE x.n fr, aUA x.n fr, aCNT x.n fr, aGT x.n fr, aTOP x.n fr]

/-- The time of the parameters. -/
def tParams (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  log2Time n + sqrtTime (kOf n) + tPow2 (ellOf n) + sqrtTime (ellOf n) + tDiv (bOf n) 2 +
    tDiv (3 * kOf n) (dOf n) + tDiv (284225 * kOf n) (10 ^ 7) + tPow2 (284225 * kOf n / 10 ^ 7) +
    tDiv (n + sOf n - 1) (sOf n) + log2Time (sOf n) + tDiv (cKOf n + bOf n) (ellOf n) +
    log2Time (3 * U) + tDiv (BOf U - 1) (ellOf n) + 400

/-- The procedures for the parameters. -/
structure ParamProcs (P : Program) (pLog pSqrt pPow pDiv : ℕ) : Prop where
  log : P[pLog]? = some log2Body
  sqrt : P[pSqrt]? = some sqrtBody
  pow : P[pPow]? = some pow2Body
  div : P[pDiv]? = some divBody

end Light.Filter
end

-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostAssemble
/-!
# The filtering host: the top procedure

After the parameters, the host sieves the primes below `2R`, keeps those of the pool, marks all
candidates and no group, and runs `core` (`top_spec`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

variable {lim : Limits}

/-- The pool, the marks and the flags, and the core.  Locals 27 `Q`, 28 scratch. -/
def restStmt (pSieve pPF pFill pCore : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .call pSieve [Light.k 2 *' Light.v 9 -' Light.k 1, Light.v 6, Light.v 26] 27 ;;
  .call pPF [Light.v 6, Light.v 27, Light.v 9, Light.v 20] 27 ;;
  .call pFill [Light.v 21, Light.v 14 *' Light.v 19, Light.k 1] 28 ;;
  .call pFill [Light.v 22, Light.v 19, Light.k 0] 28 ;;
  .call pCore [Light.v 0, Light.v 1, Light.v 2, Light.v 3, Light.v 4, Light.v 13, Light.v 20, Light.v 21, Light.v 22, Light.v 23, Light.v 24, Light.v 25, Light.v 26, Light.v 19,
    Light.v 14, Light.v 27, Light.v 18, Light.v 16, Light.v 12, Light.v 5] 28 ;;
  .set 0 (Light.k 0)

/-- The host. -/
def topBody (pLog pSqrt pPow pDiv pSieve pPF pFill pCore : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  paramsStmt pLog pSqrt pPow pDiv ;; restStmt pSieve pPF pFill pCore

/-- The time of the host. -/
def tTop (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  tParams n U + sieveTime (2 * RR n - 1) + tPoolFilter (2 * RR n) + fillTime (Light.Filter.LL n) +
    fillTime (n * n) + tCore To n U + 200

/-- The procedures of the host besides core. -/
structure TopProcs (P : Program) (pSieve pPF pFill : ℕ) : Prop where
  sieve : P[pSieve]? = some sieveBody
  pf : P[pPF]? = some poolFilterBody
  fill : P[pFill]? = some fillBody

section top

variable {P₀ R : Program} {pO pAggr pStep pFA pCert pArg pCopy : ℕ} {To : List ℕ → ℕ}
  {needo : List ℕ → Need} {d : ℕ} {x : AEInst} {fr : ℕ} {μ0 : ℕ → ℤ}

end top

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostMain
/-!
# The filtering host solves all-edges Exact Triangle

`filter_host`: from a solver of the counting oracle, the host builds a solver of all-edges Exact
Triangle, within `filterTime To` steps and with the need `filterNeed needo`; its need is
polynomially bounded if that of the oracle is.
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

/-! ## The program -/

/-- The procedures of the host, appended to a program of length `o` whose procedure `po` is the
counting oracle.  The host is procedure `o + 18`. -/
def hostProcs (o po : ℕ) : Program :=
  [aggrBody, certBody, argminBody, copyBody, filterActBody,
    stepBody po o (o + 1) (o + 2) (o + 3),
    roundBody po o (o + 5) (o + 4),
    scanBody, groupBody (o + 7), finalBody (o + 8), coreBody (o + 6) (o + 9),
    log2Body, sqrtBody, pow2Body, divBody, sieveBody, poolFilterBody, fillBody,
    Light.Filter.topBody (o + 11) (o + 12) (o + 13) (o + 14) (o + 15) (o + 16) (o + 17) (o + 10)]

/-! ## The time and the need -/

/-- **The time of the host**: the parameters, the sieve, the pool, the marks, and the core, which
runs `roundsOf n` rounds of `rOf n` steps; a step calls the oracle `QOf n` times (once per prime of
the pool) and a round twice more, each call within `supTo To n U`. -/
def filterTime (To : List ℕ → ℕ) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ := tTop To n U

/-- The largest word of the oracle at the moduli up to `Pmax`. -/
def supW (needo : List ℕ → Light.Need) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (PmaxOf n + 1)).sup fun p => (needo [n, U, sOf n, p]).word

/-- The most cells of the oracle at the moduli up to `Pmax`. -/
def supC (needo : List ℕ → Light.Need) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (PmaxOf n + 1)).sup fun p => (needo [n, U, sOf n, p]).cells

/-- The largest depth of the oracle at the moduli up to `Pmax`. -/
def supD (needo : List ℕ → Light.Need) (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (PmaxOf n + 1)).sup fun p => (needo [n, U, sOf n, p]).depth

/-- **The need of the host.** -/
def filterNeed (needo : List ℕ → Light.Need) (n U : ℕ) : Light.Need where
  word := filterWord n U + supW needo n U
  cells := aTOP n 0 + 2 * RR n + supC needo n U
  depth := supD needo n U + 5

variable {lim : Limits}

/-! ## The host solves all-edges Exact Triangle -/

/-! ## The need is polynomially bounded -/

/-- A bound on the need of the oracle at the moduli up to `Pmax`. -/
def oBound (s0 k0 n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  2 ^ s0 * ((n + 1) * ((U + 1) * ((2 * n + 2) * ((2 ^ 8 * (2 * n + 1) ^ 11 + 1) * 1)))) ^ k0

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostTime
/-!
# The time of the filtering host

`filterTime_le`: the host calls the oracle `roundsOf n * (rOf n * QOf n + 2)` times, each within
`supTo To n U`; besides, it spends `1000 (n + 1)² (Q + 1) (m + Q + 1)` steps per step of a round and
once for the final pass, `cFin n U * tScan (sOf n)` steps for the final scans (`0` under the guard,
`m n² (24 s + 35)` without it), and `tPrelude n U` steps for the parameters, the sieve, the pool and
the marks.
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

/-- The time of the parameters, the sieve, the pool and the marks. -/
def tPrelude (n U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  tParams n U + sieveTime (2 * RR n - 1) + tPoolFilter (2 * RR n) + fillTime (Light.Filter.LL n) +
    fillTime (n * n) + 300

/-- The work of one step of a round, apart from the calls of the oracle (a bound). -/
def stepWork (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 1000 * ((n + 1) ^ 2 * (QOf n + 1) * (mOf n + QOf n + 1))

end Light.Filter
end
end

records.theorem_title: APSP in $O(n^{2.996001})$: definitions, part 1 of 2
records.natural_language_statement:
Definitions for the formal proof that all-pairs shortest paths can be solved deterministically in time $O(n^{2.996001})$ on a word RAM, part 1 of 2. It imports the foundation bundles `APSPSource_*`, `TrulySubcubicAPSP_SourceSpecification` and the bundles `APSP299791_Defs*` of the 2.99791 entry.

This part contains the program `programF` of the pruned thin product at the new parameters (`ratParamsF`, the regime test $D^{1249}\le N^{71}$, time and need), the parameters of the filtering reduction (`kOf`, `ellOf`, `RR`, `bOf`, `dOf`, `roundsOf`, `sOf`, `mOf`, `rOf`, `hOf`, the prime pool `pool`, `QOf`, `Guard`, `PmaxOf`), the counts `cntOf`/`cntList` and the task `oracleTask` of the counting oracle, the oracle's procedures, data and time (`oracleProcs`, `oCoreBody`, `oTimeAt`), the masses and certificates of Lemma 3.1, and the procedures of the filtering host.

Source modules (in this order): `ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Assigns`, `ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Frames`, `ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Lib.Logs`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.ThinCosts`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.ThinRegime`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.ThinRegimeTest`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.ThinAll`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.Defs`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleData`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleScatter`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleLoop`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleCore`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleHost`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleNeedPoly`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.Asymp`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleBound`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.Mass`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostMath`, `ThreeSumApsp.Filter.HostProcs`.

The bundles belong to the formal proof of the deterministic bound $O(n^{2.996001})$ for APSP (the filtering reduction of the 2.996001 note):

1. the pruned thin product of the 2.99791 entry at the new parameters $c=212733/10000$, $\theta=111731/10^6$, in the regime $D^{1249}\le N^{71}$, giving #Lop-AE-SparseTri (counting) in time $O(n^2\log^2D/D^{0.0703531}+wD^{0.4296471}\log D+nD+w)$;
2. the modular counting oracle of Lemma 4.1: for a block size $s$ and a modulus $p$ it computes, for every pair $(a,b)$ and every block $C_j$ of $s$ third vertices, the number of $c\in C_j$ with $p\mid w(a,b)+w(b,c)+w(a,c)$, by #Lop-AE-SparseTri calls at inner dimension $sp$;
3. the deterministic filtering host (Lemma 3.1): rounds of prime moduli from a pool of primes in $[R,2R)$ that certify the pairs with an exact triangle and shrink the set of active candidates, followed by a final check, solving All-Edges Exact Triangle, and the chain to APSP.

**Formalization Note** Each bundle is generated from the library by deleting the theorems that are not needed ("skeleton subtraction"); it keeps definitions, structures and instances, and the few lemmas that the definitions themselves need, with proofs. Tactic macros of the library are expanded at their uses. Everything else is imported from the bundles `APSPSource_*`, `TrulySubcubicAPSP_SourceSpecification` and `APSP299791_Defs*`.

-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Assigns
/-!
# A statement changes only the local variables that it assigns

`s.assigns` lists the local variables that the statement `s` assigns: the targets of its
assignments and the result variables of its calls.  A run of `s` leaves every other local variable
as it was (`Exec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns`), so every fact about `s` may be extended by "all other
locals are as before" (`Ends.keeping`).  A lemma about a piece of program text therefore speaks
about the memory and about the locals that the piece assigns, and about no other local.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-- The local variables that a statement assigns: the targets of its assignments and the result
variables of its calls. -/
@[simp] def Stmt.assigns : Stmt → List ℕ
  | .skip => []
  | .set x _ => [x]
  | .store _ _ => []
  | .seq s t => s.assigns ++ t.assigns
  | .ite _ s t => s.assigns ++ t.assigns
  | .while _ s => s.assigns
  | .call _ _ x => [x]

end Light
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Frames
/-!
# Local variables as a list

In the proof of a procedure body the state is written out as ⟨frame [a, b, …], μ⟩: the list
holds the local variables 0, 1, …, and all further ones are 0.  An assignment to local x replaces
entry x of the list (setLocal).  The rules of this file treat one statement each.  They are told the
value that is assigned or stored, and they ask for one fact about each expression: that its
evaluation stays within the limits and gives this value (Expr.Gives).  This fact and the comparison
of the costs are proved by default from the hypotheses in the context.  Ends.forFrame and
Ends.forShape are the rules for counting loops in this form.  In the names of the rules, To says
that the state is ⟨frame l, μ⟩.

Locals by name, and locals whose values do not matter:

* `setLocals l [(x, a), (y, b), …]` is the list `l` after the assignments `x := a`, `y := b`, ….
  With the names of the locals for `x`, `y`, … it describes the locals of a procedure by name:
  `setLocals [] [(Size, n), (Bound, U), …]`.
* `updateLocals loc [(x, a), (y, b), …]` is the same for locals that are not given as a list.  A
  lemma about a piece of text that several procedures share is stated for arbitrary locals `loc`.
* `refreshLocals l loc xs` is the list `l` with the entries `xs` read from `loc`.
* `LocalsBut xs l loc` says that `loc` agrees with `frame l` except perhaps at the locals `xs`.  In
  an invariant, `xs` are the scratch variables.  `Ends.asFrame` goes from such locals to a list, and
  `LocalsBut.of_eq` comes back.
* `Ends.pieceTo` and `Ends.pieceToThen` use a lemma about a piece of text that assigns only the
  locals `xs`: afterwards the locals are `refreshLocals l loc' xs`, where `loc'` are the locals of
  which the lemma speaks.  The lemma need not mention the locals that the piece does not assign.
* `Ends.forScratch` is the rule for a counting loop whose body may change the scratch variables
  `xs`: the round says nothing about the locals.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-! ## The list of the locals -/

/-! ## The value of an expression -/

/-! ## One statement -/

section rules

variable {l : List ℤ} {μ : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ} {Q : State → Prop}

end rules

/-! ## Locals by name, and locals whose values do not matter -/

/-- The list `l` of the locals, with the entries `xs` read from `loc`. -/
@[simp] def refreshLocals (l : List ℤ) (loc : ℕ → ℤ) : List ℕ → List ℤ
  | [] => l
  | x :: xs => refreshLocals (setLocal l x (loc x)) loc xs

/-- The local variables `loc` are those of the list `l`, except perhaps the locals `xs`. -/
def LocalsBut (xs : List ℕ) (l : List ℤ) (loc : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ y ∉ xs, loc y = Light.frame l y

section
variable {xs : List ℕ} {l l' : List ℤ} {loc μ : ℕ → ℤ}

/-! ## A piece of program text with a lemma of its own -/

variable {T T₁ : ℕ} {s s₁ s₂ : Stmt} {Q R : State → Prop}

/-! ## Counting loops with scratch variables -/

end

end Light
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Lang.Lib.Logs
/-!
# Logarithms, the cube root and halves, without division

Four routines on local variables only; none of them touches the memory.

* log2(x) returns ⌊log₂ x⌋ (0 for x = 0) by doubling (`log2_meets`).
* clog2(x) returns ⌈log₂ x⌉ (0 for x ≤ 1) by doubling (`clog2_meets`).
* cbrtCeil(n) returns the least s with s³ ≥ n, which is ⌈n^{1/3}⌉, by counting up
  (`cbrtCeil_meets`).
* half(h) returns ⌈h/2⌉ by counting up (`half_meets`).

Each of them is one loop that tries the candidates 0, 1, 2, … in turn.  Local variable 0 holds the
argument and receives the result, local variable 1 holds the candidate (`Arg`, `Cand`), and the two
logarithms keep a power of two in local variable 2 (`Power`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

namespace Logs

@[inherit_doc Light.Logs.Arg] abbrev Power : ℕ := 2

end Logs

open Logs

/-! ## The logarithm, rounded down -/

/-- log2(x): the candidate is L, and the power is 2^(L + 1). -/
def log2Body : Stmt :=

  .set Light.Logs.Power (Light.k 2) ;;

-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.ThinRegimeTest
/-!
# The test D^1249 ≤ N^71

regimeTestF(N, D) returns 1 if `D^1249 ≤ N^71` and 0 if not, and changes no cell.  It computes
`X = N^71` by a loop of 71 multiplications (each partial power is at most `N^71`, or 0), and then
compares `D^1249` with `X` as `regimeTestP` compares `D^91` with `N^5`: by at most 1249
multiplications, none of which exceeds `X D` (but for the first product, which is `D`), stopping as
soon as a power of `D` exceeds `X`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-! ## The text -/

/-- One round of the computation of `N^71` (`N` is local 0, the power local 2, its exponent
local 3). -/
def nPowRoundF : Stmt :=
  .set 2 (Light.v 2 *' Light.v 0) ;; .set 3 (Light.v 3 +' k 1)

/-- The computation of `N^71` into local 2. -/
def nPowF : Stmt :=
  .set 2 (k 1) ;;
  .set 3 (k 0) ;;
  .while (Light.v 3 <' k 71) nPowRoundF

/-- One round of the comparison of `D^1249` with `X` (local 0; `D` is local 1, the power local 7,
its exponent local 8, the flag local 9). -/
def regimePowRoundF : Stmt :=
  .ite (Light.v 0 <' Light.v 7 *' Light.v 1)
    (.set 9 (k 0) ;; .set 8 (k 1249))
    (.set 7 (Light.v 7 *' Light.v 1) ;; .set 8 (Light.v 8 +' k 1))

/-- The test `D^1249 ≤ X`: the flag (local 9) ends as 1 if it holds and as 0 if not. -/
def regimePowF : Stmt :=
  .set 7 (k 1) ;;
  .set 8 (k 0) ;;
  .set 9 (k 1) ;;
  .while (Light.v 8 <' k 1249) regimePowRoundF

/-- regimeTestF(N, D): `X := N^71`, then the test `D^1249 ≤ X`. -/
def regimeTestFBody : Stmt :=
  nPowF ;;
  .set 0 (Light.v 2) ;;
  regimePowF ;;
  .set 0 (Light.v 9)

/-! ## The power of N -/

/-- The states of the loop that computes `N^71`. -/
def NPowInvF (N D : ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (σ : State) : Prop :=
  σ.mem = μ ∧ σ.loc 0 = N ∧ σ.loc 1 = D ∧
    ∃ j : ℕ, j ≤ 71 ∧ σ.loc 3 = j ∧ σ.loc 2 = ((N ^ j : ℕ) : ℤ)

/-! ## The comparison -/

/-- The states of the loop: as `PowInv91`, with 1249 in place of 91. -/
def PowInvF (X D : ℕ) (loc μ : ℕ → ℤ) (σ : State) : Prop :=
  σ.mem = μ ∧ (∀ x < 7, σ.loc x = loc x) ∧
    ((∃ j : ℕ, j ≤ 1249 ∧ σ.loc 8 = j ∧ σ.loc 9 = 1 ∧ σ.loc 7 = ((D ^ j : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
        (j = 0 ∨ D ^ j ≤ X)) ∨
      (σ.loc 8 = 1249 ∧ σ.loc 9 = 0 ∧ X < D ^ 1249))

/-! ## The test -/

end Light.Filter
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.Defs
/-!
# Deterministic filtering: parameters and the counting oracle

The filtering reduction of the 2.996001 note (Lemma 3.1, Lemma 4.1).  A candidate is a triple
`(a, b, j)`: the pair `(a, b)` and the block `C_j = [j s, min((j+1) s, n))` of third vertices.  It
lies at index `i = j n² + a n + b`; its group is the pair, `i % (n n) = a n + b`.  For a modulus
`p ≥ 1` its count is the number of `c ∈ C_j` with `p ∣ w(a,b) + w(b,c) + w(a,c)`.

* The parameters, as functions of `n` and `U` (§3, (3.5)): `kOf`, `ellOf`, `RR`, `bOf`, `dOf`,
  `roundsOf`, `sOf`, `mOf`, `cKOf`, `rOf`, `BOf`, `hOf`, `pool`, `QOf`, `Guard`, `PmaxOf`.
* The counts (`cntList`) and the task of the counting oracle (`oracleTask`).
-/

@[expose] public section

open ThreeSumApsp

namespace Light.Filter

open ThreeSumApsp.Spec Light.Sec3

/-! ## Parameters -/

/-- `k`, the bit length of `n`: `n < 2^k`. -/
def kOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size n

/-- `ℓ = ⌊√k⌋ + 1`. -/
def ellOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt (kOf n) + 1

/-- `R = 2^ℓ`; the pool is the primes in `[R, 2R)`. -/
def RR (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ ellOf n

/-- `b = ℓ (⌊√ℓ⌋ + 1)`, about `k^{3/4}`. -/
def bOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ellOf n * (Nat.sqrt (ellOf n) + 1)

/-- `d = ⌊b/2⌋`: a round with the guard shrinks the active set by `2^d`. -/
def dOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := bOf n / 2

/-- The number of rounds, `⌊3k/d⌋ + 1`, so that `d · rounds > 3k`. -/
def roundsOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 3 * kOf n / dOf n + 1

/-- The block size `s = 2^{⌊σ k⌋}`, `σ = 0.0284225`. -/
def sOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ (284225 * kOf n / 10 ^ 7)

/-- The number of blocks, `⌈n/s⌉`. -/
def mOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (n + sOf n - 1) / sOf n

/-- `c_K`, the bit length of the largest witness count `s`. -/
def cKOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size (sOf n)

/-- The number of prime factors per round, `⌊(c_K + b)/ℓ⌋ + 1`. -/
def rOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (cKOf n + bOf n) / ellOf n + 1

/-- `B`, the bit length of `3U`: every triangle sum has absolute value below `2^B`. -/
def BOf (U : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size (3 * U)

/-- `h = ⌊(B − 1)/ℓ⌋`: a nonzero integer below `2^B` in absolute value has at most `h` prime
divisors in the pool. -/
def hOf (n U : ℕ) : ℕ := (BOf U - 1) / ellOf n

/-- The pool: the primes in `[R, 2R)`. -/
def pool (n : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (2 * RR n)).filter fun q => RR n ≤ q ∧ q.Prime

/-- `Q`, the size of the pool. -/
def QOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Light.Filter.pool n).card

/-- The guard (3.6), `K (2h)^r 2^d ≤ Q^r` with `K = s`.  Not tested by the program on the main
path; it holds for all large `n` along polynomially bounded `U`. -/
def Guard (n U : ℕ) : Prop := sOf n * (2 * hOf n U) ^ rOf n * 2 ^ dOf n ≤ QOf n ^ rOf n

instance (n U : ℕ) : Decidable (Guard n U) := by unfold Guard; infer_instance

/-- The largest modulus, `(2R)^r`. -/
def PmaxOf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (2 * RR n) ^ rOf n

/-! ## The counts -/

/-- The block `j` of third vertices: `c` with `j s ≤ c < (j + 1) s` and `c < n`. -/
def InBlock (n s j c : ℕ) : Prop := j * s ≤ c ∧ c < (j + 1) * s ∧ c < n

instance (n s j c : ℕ) : Decidable (InBlock n s j c) := by unfold InBlock; infer_instance

/-- The triangle sum `w(a,b) + w(b,c) + w(a,c)` of the pair `q = a n + b` and the vertex `c`, as in
`aeFlags`. -/
def triSum (n : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (q c : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  AB.getD q 0 + BC.getD (q % n * n + c) 0 + AC.getD (q / n * n + c) 0

/-- The count of the candidate `i = j n² + q` at the modulus `p`: the `c` in block `j` with
`p ∣ triSum q c`. -/
def cntOf (n s p : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range n).filter fun c =>
    InBlock n s (i / (n * n)) c ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ triSum n AB BC AC (i % (n * n)) c).card

/-- All `m n²` counts at the modulus `p`, candidate `i` in cell `i`. -/
def cntList (n s p : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) : List ℤ :=
  (List.range ((n + s - 1) / s * (n * n))).map fun i => (cntOf n s p AB BC AC i : ℤ)

/-! ## The counting oracle as a task -/

/-- An instance of the oracle: an all-edges instance (without the place of the flags), a block size
`s`, a modulus `p`, and the place `cnt` of the `m n²` counts. -/
structure OracleInst : Type extends TriInst where
  s : ℕ
  p : ℕ
  cnt : ℕ

/-- The number of counts, `⌈n/s⌉ n²`. -/
def OracleInst.len (x : OracleInst) : ℕ := (x.n + x.s - 1) / x.s * (x.n * x.n)

/-- The matrices and the place of the counts lie below the free pointer and do not meet;
`1 ≤ s ≤ n`, `1 ≤ p`. -/
structure OracleInst.Pre (x : OracleInst) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (fr : ℕ) : Prop
    extends TriInst.Pre x.toTriInst μ fr where
  s_pos : 1 ≤ x.s
  s_le : x.s ≤ x.n
  p_pos : 1 ≤ x.p
  belowCnt : x.cnt + x.len ≤ fr
  apartAB : Apart x.ab (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len
  apartBC : Apart x.bc (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len
  apartAC : Apart x.ac (x.n * x.n) x.cnt x.len

/-- **The counting oracle** (Lemma 4.1): `oracle(n, U, ab, bc, ac, s, p, cnt, fr)` writes the counts
of all candidates at the modulus `p` to `cnt`, and changes no other cell below `fr`. -/
def oracleTask : TaskN where
  Inst := OracleInst
  pars x := [x.n, x.U, x.s, x.p]
  args x := [x.n, x.U, x.ab, x.bc, x.ac, x.s, x.p, x.cnt]
  Pre := OracleInst.Pre
  Post x μ fr _ μ' := Seg μ' x.cnt (cntList x.n x.s x.p x.AB x.BC x.AC) ∧
    KeptBut μ μ' fr x.cnt x.len

end Light.Filter
end
end

section
-- Source module: ThreeSumApsp.Filter.OracleData
/-!
# The counting oracle (Lemma 4.1): its instances, as pure data

The oracle reuses the instances of the host of Theorem 17 (`HostData`): the block size `s` plays the
part of the piece size `q`, the inner dimension is `D = s p`, and a class `W_ϱ` of the pairs is cut

/-- The data of the instances of the oracle. -/
def oData (n s p : ℕ) (AB BC AC : List ℤ) : HostData := ⟨n, s * p, p, s, oCap n p, AB, BC, AC⟩

open HostData

variable {X : HostData}
